title: arxiv_1902.10106v1
universal_lens: Observational causal inference framework linking high school football participation to late-adulthood health outcomes via matched control groups and confounder adjustment. A probabilistic framework linking childhood socioeconomic status and physical activity patterns to adult self-rated health through longitudinal cohort data.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian hierarchical modeling of health outcomes with matching adjustments and sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding using conformal prediction intervals. Bayesian causal inference models adjust for confounders using WLS covariates to estimate posterior distributions over health outcomes at age 65.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state-transition dynamics from youth athletic exposure to adult health states, incorporating temporal causality and intervention thresholds. Situationally grounded state transitions map from adolescent activity levels and family SES into adult health states via dynamic decision trees and reinforcement learning.

primitives.name: Observational Study Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Methods and Analysis: Our proposed study is a retrospective observational study that compares 1,153 high school males who played varsity football with 2,751 male students who did not.
primitives.assumptions: Study population is representative of U.S. high school males; outcomes are measurable at age 65; confounders are partially observed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Retrospective cohort comparison with matching controls.

layer2.mapping: The observational protocol maps to a Bayesian causal graph where football participation is a treatment variable and health outcomes are response variables.
layer2.telemetry: Matched pair ratios and outcome prevalence across groups.

primitives.name: Confounding Adjustment Methodology
primitives.verbatim_quote: To control for potential confounders, we adjust for pre-exposure covariates with matching and model-based covariance adjustment.
primitives.assumptions: Pre-exposure covariates are sufficient to explain confounding; matching reduces selection bias.

layer2.mapping: Adjustment kernel derived from inverse probability weighting and propensity score matching for causal effect estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Standardized mean difference before and after adjustment.
